# provider-cloudnative-pg reference

Every value users can set on an Instance, a Backup or a Restore of this provider, with its
type, constraints and description. The provider's admission webhook checks them against
the same schemas, which the `Provider` and `BackupClass` resources publish
(`kubectl get provider provider-cloudnative-pg -o yaml`).

The fields of the Instance itself (`spec.version`, `spec.components.<name>.replicas`,
`resources`, `storage`, `schedulingPolicy`, `spec.dataSource`, ...) are OpenEverest's:
`kubectl explain instance.spec`.

- [Versions](#versions)
- [Topologies](#topologies)
- [Component engine (postgresql)](#component-engine-postgresql)
- [Component proxy (pgbouncer)](#component-proxy-pgbouncer)
- [Topology replicaSet](#topology-replicaset)
- [BackupClass cnpg-barman-plugin: backups](#backupclass-cnpg-barman-plugin-backups)

## Versions

`spec.version` of an Instance selects one of these releases (default `18.7`).

| Version | engine |
|---|---|
| `18.7` | 18.7 (`ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.7-standard-trixie`) |
| `18.6` | 18.6 (`ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.6-standard-trixie`) |
| `18.4` | 18.4 (`ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.4-standard-trixie`) |
| `17.10` | 17.10 (`ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:17.10-standard-trixie`) |
| `16.14` | 16.14 (`ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:16.14-standard-trixie`) |
| `15.18` | 15.18 (`ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:15.18-standard-trixie`) |
| `14.23` | 14.23 (`ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:14.23-standard-trixie`) |

## Topologies

`spec.topology.type` of an Instance, and the components it has under `spec.components`.

| Topology | Component | Type | Optional |
|---|---|---|---|
| `replicaSet` | `engine` | postgresql |  |
| `replicaSet` | `proxy` | pgbouncer | yes |

## Component engine (postgresql)

Set in `spec.components.engine.parameters` of an Instance.

### `affinity`

`object`

Affinity is CNPG's scheduling configuration of the instance pods:
anti-affinity between instances, node selector, tolerations and
additional affinity rules. Cannot be combined with the engine's
schedulingPolicy affinity, nodeSelector or tolerations, which also set it.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity`

`object`

AdditionalPodAffinity allows to specify pod affinity terms to be passed to all the cluster's pods.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`

`[]object`

The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy
the affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose
a node that violates one or more of the expressions. The node that is
most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e.
for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource
request, requiredDuringScheduling affinity expressions, etc.),
compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and adding
"weight" to the sum if the node has pods which matches the corresponding podAffinityTerm; the
node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm`

`object` · required

Required. A pod affinity term, associated with the corresponding weight.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.labelSelector`

`object`

A label query over a set of resources, in this case pods.
If it's null, this PodAffinityTerm matches with no Pods.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.labelSelector.matchExpressions`

`[]object`

matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.labelSelector.matchExpressions[].key`

`string` · required

key is the label key that the selector applies to.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.labelSelector.matchExpressions[].operator`

`string` · required

operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.labelSelector.matchExpressions[].values`

`[]string`

values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. This array is replaced during a strategic
merge patch.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.labelSelector.matchLabels`

`map[string]string`

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels
map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the
operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.matchLabelKeys`

`[]string`

MatchLabelKeys is a set of pod label keys to select which pods will
be taken into consideration. The keys are used to lookup values from the
incoming pod labels, those key-value labels are merged with `labelSelector` as `key in (value)`
to select the group of existing pods which pods will be taken into consideration
for the incoming pod's pod (anti) affinity. Keys that don't exist in the incoming
pod labels will be ignored. The default value is empty.
The same key is forbidden to exist in both matchLabelKeys and labelSelector.
Also, matchLabelKeys cannot be set when labelSelector isn't set.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.mismatchLabelKeys`

`[]string`

MismatchLabelKeys is a set of pod label keys to select which pods will
be taken into consideration. The keys are used to lookup values from the
incoming pod labels, those key-value labels are merged with `labelSelector` as `key notin (value)`
to select the group of existing pods which pods will be taken into consideration
for the incoming pod's pod (anti) affinity. Keys that don't exist in the incoming
pod labels will be ignored. The default value is empty.
The same key is forbidden to exist in both mismatchLabelKeys and labelSelector.
Also, mismatchLabelKeys cannot be set when labelSelector isn't set.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.namespaceSelector`

`object`

A label query over the set of namespaces that the term applies to.
The term is applied to the union of the namespaces selected by this field
and the ones listed in the namespaces field.
null selector and null or empty namespaces list means "this pod's namespace".
An empty selector ({}) matches all namespaces.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.namespaceSelector.matchExpressions`

`[]object`

matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.namespaceSelector.matchExpressions[].key`

`string` · required

key is the label key that the selector applies to.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.namespaceSelector.matchExpressions[].operator`

`string` · required

operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.namespaceSelector.matchExpressions[].values`

`[]string`

values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. This array is replaced during a strategic
merge patch.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.namespaceSelector.matchLabels`

`map[string]string`

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels
map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the
operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.namespaces`

`[]string`

namespaces specifies a static list of namespace names that the term applies to.
The term is applied to the union of the namespaces listed in this field
and the ones selected by namespaceSelector.
null or empty namespaces list and null namespaceSelector means "this pod's namespace".

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].podAffinityTerm.topologyKey`

`string` · required

This pod should be co-located (affinity) or not co-located (anti-affinity) with the pods matching
the labelSelector in the specified namespaces, where co-located is defined as running on a node
whose value of the label with key topologyKey matches that of any node on which any of the
selected pods is running.
Empty topologyKey is not allowed.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].weight`

`integer (int32)` · required

weight associated with matching the corresponding podAffinityTerm,
in the range 1-100.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`

`[]object`

If the affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at
scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node.
If the affinity requirements specified by this field cease to be met
at some point during pod execution (e.g. due to a pod label update), the
system may or may not try to eventually evict the pod from its node.
When there are multiple elements, the lists of nodes corresponding to each
podAffinityTerm are intersected, i.e. all terms must be satisfied.

#### `affinity.additionalPodAntiAffinity`

`object`

by the operator if EnablePodAntiAffinity is set to true (default) or to be used exclusively if set to false.

#### `affinity.enablePodAntiAffinity`

`boolean`

Activates anti-affinity for the pods. The operator will define pods
anti-affinity unless this field is explicitly set to false

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity`

`object`

NodeAffinity describes node affinity scheduling rules for the pod.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#node-affinity

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`

most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e.
for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource
request, requiredDuringScheduling affinity expressions, etc.),
compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and adding
"weight" to the sum if the node matches the corresponding matchExpressions; the
node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference`

`object` · required

A node selector term, associated with the corresponding weight.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference.matchExpressions`

`[]object`

A list of node selector requirements by node's labels.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference.matchExpressions[].key`

`string` · required

The label key that the selector applies to.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference.matchExpressions[].operator`

`string` · required

Represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist. Gt, and Lt.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference.matchExpressions[].values`

`[]string`

An array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. If the operator is Gt or Lt, the values
array must have a single element, which will be interpreted as an integer.
This array is replaced during a strategic merge patch.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference.matchFields`

`[]object`

A list of node selector requirements by node's fields.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference.matchFields[].key`

`string` · required

The label key that the selector applies to.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference.matchFields[].operator`

`string` · required

Represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist. Gt, and Lt.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].preference.matchFields[].values`

`[]string`

An array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. If the operator is Gt or Lt, the values
array must have a single element, which will be interpreted as an integer.
This array is replaced during a strategic merge patch.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[].weight`

`integer (int32)` · required

Weight associated with matching the corresponding nodeSelectorTerm, in the range 1-100.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`

`object`

If the affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at
scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node.
If the affinity requirements specified by this field cease to be met
at some point during pod execution (e.g. due to an update), the system
may or may not try to eventually evict the pod from its node.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms`

`[]object` · required

Required. A list of node selector terms. The terms are ORed.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchExpressions`

`[]object`

A list of node selector requirements by node's labels.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchExpressions[].key`

`string` · required

The label key that the selector applies to.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchExpressions[].operator`

`string` · required

Represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist. Gt, and Lt.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchExpressions[].values`

`[]string`

An array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. If the operator is Gt or Lt, the values
array must have a single element, which will be interpreted as an integer.
This array is replaced during a strategic merge patch.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchFields`

`[]object`

A list of node selector requirements by node's fields.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchFields[].key`

`string` · required

The label key that the selector applies to.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchFields[].operator`

`string` · required

Represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist. Gt, and Lt.

#### `affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchFields[].values`

`[]string`

An array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. If the operator is Gt or Lt, the values
array must have a single element, which will be interpreted as an integer.
This array is replaced during a strategic merge patch.

#### `affinity.nodeSelector`

`map[string]string`

NodeSelector is map of key-value pairs used to define the nodes on which
the pods can run.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/

#### `affinity.podAntiAffinityType`

`string`

PodAntiAffinityType allows the user to decide whether pod anti-affinity between cluster instance has to be
considered a strong requirement during scheduling or not. Allowed values are: "preferred" (default if empty) or
"required". Setting it to "required", could lead to instances remaining pending until new kubernetes nodes are
added if all the existing nodes don't match the required pod anti-affinity rule.
More info:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#inter-pod-affinity-and-anti-affinity

#### `affinity.tolerations`

`[]object`

Tolerations is a list of Tolerations that should be set for all the pods, in order to allow them to run
on tainted nodes.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/

#### `affinity.tolerations[].effect`

`string`

Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects.
When specified, allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule and NoExecute.

#### `affinity.tolerations[].key`

`string`

Key is the taint key that the toleration applies to. Empty means match all taint keys.
If the key is empty, operator must be Exists; this combination means to match all values and all keys.

#### `affinity.tolerations[].operator`

`string`

Operator represents a key's relationship to the value.
Valid operators are Exists, Equal, Lt, and Gt. Defaults to Equal.
Exists is equivalent to wildcard for value, so that a pod can
tolerate all taints of a particular category.
Lt and Gt perform numeric comparisons (requires feature gate TaintTolerationComparisonOperators).

#### `affinity.tolerations[].tolerationSeconds`

`integer (int64)`

TolerationSeconds represents the period of time the toleration (which must be
of effect NoExecute, otherwise this field is ignored) tolerates the taint. By default,
it is not set, which means tolerate the taint forever (do not evict). Zero and
negative values will be treated as 0 (evict immediately) by the system.

#### `affinity.tolerations[].value`

`string`

Value is the taint value the toleration matches to.
If the operator is Exists, the value should be empty, otherwise just a regular string.

#### `affinity.topologyKey`

`string`

TopologyKey to use for anti-affinity configuration. See k8s documentation
for more info on that

### `bootstrap`

`object`

Bootstrap sets how a new instance is initialized. Only read at
creation, and ignored when the Instance restores a backup
(spec.dataSource).

#### `bootstrap.initdb`

`object`

InitDB is CNPG's initdb bootstrap: the application database and its
owner (both CNPG's default, app, when unset; set both or neither), the
Secret with the owner's password, locale and encoding, and SQL to run
after initialization.

- Rule: builtinLocale is only available when localeProvider is set to `builtin` (`!has(self.builtinLocale) || self.localeProvider == 'builtin'`)
- Rule: icuLocale is only available when localeProvider is set to `icu` (`!has(self.icuLocale) || self.localeProvider == 'icu'`)
- Rule: icuRules is only available when localeProvider is set to `icu` (`!has(self.icuRules) || self.localeProvider == 'icu'`)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.builtinLocale`

`string`

Specifies the locale name when the builtin provider is used.
This option requires `localeProvider` to be set to `builtin`.
Available from PostgreSQL 17.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.dataChecksums`

`boolean`

Whether data checksums are enabled on data pages, to help detect
corruption by the I/O system that would otherwise be silent
(default: `false` before PostgreSQL 18, `true` from PostgreSQL 18 on,
matching the initdb default in each case).

#### `bootstrap.initdb.database`

`string`

Name of the database used by the application. Default: `app`.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.encoding`

`string`

The value to be passed as option `--encoding` for initdb (default:`UTF8`)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.icuLocale`

`string`

Specifies the ICU locale when the ICU provider is used.
This option requires `localeProvider` to be set to `icu`.
Available from PostgreSQL 15.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.icuRules`

`string`

Specifies additional collation rules to customize the behavior of the default collation.
This option requires `localeProvider` to be set to `icu`.
Available from PostgreSQL 16.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import`

`object`

Bootstraps the new cluster by importing data from an existing PostgreSQL
instance using logical backup (`pg_dump` and `pg_restore`)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.databases`

`[]string` · required

The databases to import

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.pgDumpExtraOptions`

`[]string`

List of custom options to pass to the `pg_dump` command.

IMPORTANT: Use with caution. The operator does not validate these options,
and certain flags may interfere with its intended functionality or design.
You are responsible for ensuring that the provided options are compatible
with your environment and desired behavior.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.pgRestoreDataOptions`

`[]string`

Custom options to pass to the `pg_restore` command during the `data`
section. This setting overrides the generic `pgRestoreExtraOptions` value.

IMPORTANT: Use with caution. The operator does not validate these options,
and certain flags may interfere with its intended functionality or design.
You are responsible for ensuring that the provided options are compatible
with your environment and desired behavior.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.pgRestoreExtraOptions`

`[]string`

List of custom options to pass to the `pg_restore` command.

IMPORTANT: Use with caution. The operator does not validate these options,
and certain flags may interfere with its intended functionality or design.
You are responsible for ensuring that the provided options are compatible
with your environment and desired behavior.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.pgRestorePostdataOptions`

`[]string`

Custom options to pass to the `pg_restore` command during the `post-data`
section. This setting overrides the generic `pgRestoreExtraOptions` value.

IMPORTANT: Use with caution. The operator does not validate these options,
and certain flags may interfere with its intended functionality or design.
You are responsible for ensuring that the provided options are compatible
with your environment and desired behavior.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.pgRestorePredataOptions`

`[]string`

Custom options to pass to the `pg_restore` command during the `pre-data`
section. This setting overrides the generic `pgRestoreExtraOptions` value.

IMPORTANT: Use with caution. The operator does not validate these options,
and certain flags may interfere with its intended functionality or design.
You are responsible for ensuring that the provided options are compatible
with your environment and desired behavior.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.postImportApplicationSQL`

`[]string`

List of SQL queries to be executed as a superuser in the application
database right after is imported - to be used with extreme care
(by default empty). Only available in microservice type.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.roles`

`[]string`

The roles to import

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.schemaOnly`

`boolean`

When set to true, only the `pre-data` and `post-data` sections of
`pg_restore` are invoked, avoiding data import. Default: `false`.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.source`

`object` · required

The source of the import

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.source.externalCluster`

`string` · required

The name of the externalCluster used for import

#### `bootstrap.initdb.import.type`

`string` · required · one of `microservice`, `monolith`

The import type. Can be `microservice` or `monolith`.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.locale`

`string`

Sets the default collation order and character classification in the new database.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.localeCType`

`string`

The value to be passed as option `--lc-ctype` for initdb (default:`C`)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.localeCollate`

`string`

The value to be passed as option `--lc-collate` for initdb (default:`C`)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.localeProvider`

`string`

This option sets the locale provider for databases created in the new cluster.
Available from PostgreSQL 16.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.options`

`[]string`

The list of options that must be passed to initdb when creating the cluster.

Deprecated: This could lead to inconsistent configurations,
please use the explicit provided parameters instead.
If defined, explicit values will be ignored.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.owner`

`string`

Name of the owner of the database in the instance to be used
by applications. Defaults to the value of the `database` key.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitApplicationSQL`

`[]string`

List of SQL queries to be executed as a superuser in the application
database right after the cluster has been created - to be used with extreme care
(by default empty)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitApplicationSQLRefs`

`object`

List of references to ConfigMaps or Secrets containing SQL files
to be executed as a superuser in the application database right after
the cluster has been created. The references are processed in a specific order:
first, all Secrets are processed, followed by all ConfigMaps.
Within each group, the processing order follows the sequence specified
in their respective arrays.
(by default empty)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitApplicationSQLRefs.configMapRefs`

`[]object`

ConfigMapRefs holds a list of references to ConfigMaps

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitApplicationSQLRefs.configMapRefs[].key`

`string` · required

The key to select

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitApplicationSQLRefs.configMapRefs[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitApplicationSQLRefs.secretRefs`

`[]object`

SecretRefs holds a list of references to Secrets

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitApplicationSQLRefs.secretRefs[].key`

`string` · required

The key to select

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitApplicationSQLRefs.secretRefs[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitSQL`

`[]string`

List of SQL queries to be executed as a superuser in the `postgres`
database right after the cluster has been created - to be used with extreme care
(by default empty)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitSQLRefs`

`object`

List of references to ConfigMaps or Secrets containing SQL files
to be executed as a superuser in the `postgres` database right after
the cluster has been created. The references are processed in a specific order:
first, all Secrets are processed, followed by all ConfigMaps.
Within each group, the processing order follows the sequence specified
in their respective arrays.
(by default empty)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitSQLRefs.configMapRefs`

`[]object`

ConfigMapRefs holds a list of references to ConfigMaps

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitSQLRefs.configMapRefs[].key`

`string` · required

The key to select

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitSQLRefs.configMapRefs[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitSQLRefs.secretRefs`

`[]object`

SecretRefs holds a list of references to Secrets

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitSQLRefs.secretRefs[].key`

`string` · required

The key to select

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitSQLRefs.secretRefs[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitTemplateSQL`

`[]string`

List of SQL queries to be executed as a superuser in the `template1`
database right after the cluster has been created - to be used with extreme care
(by default empty)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitTemplateSQLRefs`

`object`

List of references to ConfigMaps or Secrets containing SQL files
to be executed as a superuser in the `template1` database right after
the cluster has been created. The references are processed in a specific order:
first, all Secrets are processed, followed by all ConfigMaps.
Within each group, the processing order follows the sequence specified
in their respective arrays.
(by default empty)

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitTemplateSQLRefs.configMapRefs`

`[]object`

ConfigMapRefs holds a list of references to ConfigMaps

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitTemplateSQLRefs.configMapRefs[].key`

`string` · required

The key to select

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitTemplateSQLRefs.configMapRefs[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitTemplateSQLRefs.secretRefs`

`[]object`

SecretRefs holds a list of references to Secrets

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitTemplateSQLRefs.secretRefs[].key`

`string` · required

The key to select

#### `bootstrap.initdb.postInitTemplateSQLRefs.secretRefs[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.secret`

`object`

Name of the secret containing the initial credentials for the
owner of the user database. If empty a new secret will be
created from scratch

#### `bootstrap.initdb.secret.name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `bootstrap.initdb.walSegmentSize`

`integer` · minimum 1 · maximum 1024

The value in megabytes (1 to 1024) to be passed to the `--wal-segsize`
option for initdb (default: empty, resulting in PostgreSQL default: 16MB)

#### `bootstrap.volumeSnapshot`

`object`

VolumeSnapshot starts the instance from a VolumeSnapshot of another
instance's data volume, in the same namespace, instead of an empty
database. The snapshot must hold PGDATA and its WAL (no walStorage) and
can be crash-consistent: PostgreSQL recovers it from its own pg_wal, as
after a crash. On storage whose snapshots are copy-on-write clones, such
as ZFS, the instance starts in seconds whatever the size. Only read at
creation; initdb's database and owner name the existing application
database and owner.

#### `bootstrap.volumeSnapshot.name`

`string` · required

Name of the VolumeSnapshot.

### `certificates`

`object`

Certificates are the TLS certificates of the instance (CNPG
certificates). Without them CNPG issues and rotates its own.
serverTLSSecret needs serverCASecret and cannot be combined with
serverAltDNSNames; replicationTLSSecret needs clientCASecret.

#### `certificates.clientCASecret`

`string`

The secret containing the Client CA certificate. If not defined, a new secret will be created
with a self-signed CA and will be used to generate all the client certificates.&lt;br /&gt;
&lt;br /&gt;
Contains:&lt;br /&gt;
&lt;br /&gt;
- `ca.crt`: CA that should be used to validate the client certificates,

used as `ssl_ca_file` of all the instances.&lt;br /&gt;
- `ca.key`: key used to generate client certificates, if ReplicationTLSSecret is provided,

this can be omitted.&lt;br /&gt;

#### `certificates.replicationTLSSecret`

`string`

The secret of type kubernetes.io/tls containing the client certificate to authenticate as
the `streaming_replica` user.
If not defined, ClientCASecret must provide also `ca.key`, and a new secret will be
created using the provided CA.

#### `certificates.serverAltDNSNames`

`[]string`

The list of the server alternative DNS names to be added to the generated server TLS certificates, when required.

#### `certificates.serverCASecret`

`string`

The secret containing the Server CA certificate. If not defined, a new secret will be created
with a self-signed CA and will be used to generate the TLS certificate ServerTLSSecret.&lt;br /&gt;
&lt;br /&gt;
Contains:&lt;br /&gt;
&lt;br /&gt;
- `ca.crt`: CA that should be used to validate the server certificate,

used as `sslrootcert` in client connection strings.&lt;br /&gt;
- `ca.key`: key used to generate Server SSL certs, if ServerTLSSecret is provided,

this can be omitted.&lt;br /&gt;

#### `certificates.serverTLSSecret`

`string`

The secret of type kubernetes.io/tls containing the server TLS certificate and key that will be set as
`ssl_cert_file` and `ssl_key_file` so that clients can connect to postgres securely.
If not defined, ServerCASecret must provide also `ca.key` and a new secret will be
created using the provided CA.

### `extensions`

`object`

Extensions configures first-class PostgreSQL extensions managed by this provider.

#### `extensions.age`

`object`

AGE (image volume, Apache AGE graph database) preloads age, runs CREATE
EXTENSION age in the application database and grants its owner USAGE on
ag_catalog. Can only be enabled at creation; cannot be turned off.

#### `extensions.age.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.pgStatStatements`

`object`

PgStatStatements tracks planning and execution statistics of all SQL
statements (pg_stat_statements) and exports the top statements as
metrics. It ships in the standard images; the operator preloads and
creates it in every database while a pg_stat_statements.\* parameter is
set, so the provider defaults pg_stat_statements.track to "top". Enabled
by default on new instances; instances created without it keep it off
until it is enabled. Turning it on or off restarts the instances.

#### `extensions.pgStatStatements.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.pgaudit`

`object`

PgAudit enables audit logging. It ships in the standard images; the operator
preloads and creates it in every database while a pgaudit.\* parameter is
set, so the provider defaults pgaudit.log to "ddl, role". Can be turned off.

#### `extensions.pgaudit.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.pgcron`

`object`

PgCron (image volume) preloads pg_cron, sets cron.database_name to the
application database and cron.use_background_workers to on, runs CREATE
EXTENSION pg_cron there and grants its owner USAGE on the cron schema, so
the owner can schedule jobs. Jobs run on the primary only. Can only be
enabled at creation; cannot be turned off.

#### `extensions.pgcron.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.pgivm`

`object`

PgIVM (image volume) preloads pg_ivm and runs CREATE EXTENSION pg_ivm in the
application database. Cannot be turned off once enabled.

#### `extensions.pgivm.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.pgpartman`

`object`

PgPartman (image volume) preloads the pg_partman background worker, runs
CREATE EXTENSION pg_partman in the partman schema of the application
database and grants its owner the privileges to manage partitions. The
worker runs maintenance for that database as the owner
(pg_partman_bgw.dbname and pg_partman_bgw.role), on the primary only.
Requires PostgreSQL 18.7+. Can only be enabled at creation; cannot be
turned off.

#### `extensions.pgpartman.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.pgrepack`

`object`

PgRepack (image volume) runs CREATE EXTENSION pg_repack in the
application database. The pg_repack client is in the instance pods at
/extensions/pg-repack/bin/pg_repack and runs as the superuser. Cannot be
turned off once enabled.

#### `extensions.pgrepack.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.pgrouting`

`object`

PgRouting (image volume) runs CREATE EXTENSION pgrouting in the application
database. Requires postgis. Cannot be turned off once enabled.

#### `extensions.pgrouting.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.pgvector`

`object`

PgVector runs CREATE EXTENSION vector in the application database. It ships
in the CloudNativePG standard images (PostgreSQL 14+), so no image change or
restart is needed. Cannot be turned off once enabled.

#### `extensions.pgvector.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.postgis`

`object`

PostGIS (image volume) runs CREATE EXTENSION postgis in the application
database. Cannot be turned off once enabled.

#### `extensions.postgis.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.timescaledb`

`object`

TimescaleDB (image volume, Apache-2.0 edition) runs CREATE EXTENSION
timescaledb in the application database. Cannot be turned off once enabled.

#### `extensions.timescaledb.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.timescaledbCommunity`

`object`

TimescaleDBCommunity (image volume, Community Edition) is TimescaleDB with
the Timescale License (TSL) components such as compression and continuous
aggregates. The TSL is not open source: it allows internal use but
prohibits offering TimescaleDB to third parties as a database service.
Requires PostgreSQL 18.6+; cannot be combined with timescaledb. Can only
be enabled at creation; cannot be turned off.

#### `extensions.timescaledbCommunity.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

#### `extensions.wal2json`

`object`

Wal2JSON (image volume) makes the wal2json logical decoding output plugin
available to replication slots. There is no CREATE EXTENSION.

#### `extensions.wal2json.enabled`

`boolean` · required

Enabled turns the extension on. Whether it can be turned off again,
or only enabled at creation, depends on the extension.

### `managed`

`object`

Managed is CNPG's declarative management of PostgreSQL roles
(managed.roles) and of the instance's Services (managed.services). The
Instance is Provisioning until CNPG has reconciled every role, and
Failed while one cannot be.

#### `managed.roles`

`[]object`

Database roles managed by the `Cluster`

#### `managed.roles[].bypassrls`

`boolean`

Whether a role bypasses every row-level security (RLS) policy.
Default is `false`.

#### `managed.roles[].comment`

`string`

Description of the role

#### `managed.roles[].connectionLimit`

`integer (int64)` · default `-1`

If the role can log in, this specifies how many concurrent
connections the role can make. `-1` (the default) means no limit.

#### `managed.roles[].createdb`

`boolean`

When set to `true`, the role being defined will be allowed to create
new databases. Specifying `false` (default) will deny a role the
ability to create databases.

#### `managed.roles[].createrole`

`boolean`

Whether the role will be permitted to create, alter, drop, comment
on, change the security label for, and grant or revoke membership in
other roles. Default is `false`.

#### `managed.roles[].disablePassword`

`boolean`

DisablePassword indicates that a role's password should be set to NULL in Postgres

#### `managed.roles[].ensure`

`string` · default `"present"` · one of `present`, `absent`

Ensure the role is `present` or `absent` - defaults to "present"

#### `managed.roles[].inRoles`

`[]string`

List of one or more existing roles to which this role will be
immediately added as a new member. Default empty.
Changes to the list are applied to an existing role through
`GRANT` and `REVOKE` statements, not only at role creation.

#### `managed.roles[].inherit`

`boolean` · default `true`

Whether a role "inherits" the privileges of roles it is a member of.
Default is `true`.

#### `managed.roles[].login`

`boolean`

Whether the role is allowed to log in. A role having the `login`
attribute can be thought of as a user. Roles without this attribute
are useful for managing database privileges, but are not users in
the usual sense of the word. Default is `false`.

#### `managed.roles[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the role

#### `managed.roles[].passwordSecret`

`object`

Secret containing the password of the role (if present).
If null, the password will be ignored unless DisablePassword is set.
When set, the secret must follow the `kubernetes.io/basic-auth` format
and contain both a `username` and a `password` field.

#### `managed.roles[].passwordSecret.name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `managed.roles[].replication`

`boolean`

Whether a role is a replication role. A role must have this
attribute (or be a superuser) in order to be able to connect to the
server in replication mode (physical or logical replication) and in
order to be able to create or drop replication slots. A role having
the `replication` attribute is a very highly privileged role, and
should only be used on roles actually used for replication. Default
is `false`.

#### `managed.roles[].superuser`

`boolean`

Whether the role is a `superuser` who can override all access
restrictions within the database - superuser status is dangerous and
should be used only when really needed. You must yourself be a
superuser to create a new superuser. Defaults is `false`.

#### `managed.roles[].validUntil`

`string (date-time)`

Date and time after which the role's password is no longer valid.
When omitted, the password will never expire (default).

#### `managed.services`

`object`

Services roles managed by the `Cluster`

#### `managed.services.additional`

`[]object`

Additional is a list of additional managed services specified by the user.

#### `managed.services.additional[].selectorType`

`string` · required · one of `rw`, `r`, `ro`

SelectorType specifies the type of selectors that the service will have.
Valid values are "rw", "r", and "ro", representing read-write, read, and read-only services.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate`

`object` · required

ServiceTemplate is the template specification for the service.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.metadata`

`object`

Standard object's metadata.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.metadata.annotations`

`map[string]string`

Annotations is an unstructured key value map stored with a resource that may be
set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata. They are not
queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.
More info: http://kubernetes.io/docs/user-guide/annotations

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.metadata.labels`

`map[string]string`

Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize
(scope and select) objects. May match selectors of replication controllers
and services.
More info: http://kubernetes.io/docs/user-guide/labels

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.metadata.name`

`string`

The name of the resource. Only supported for certain types

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec`

`object`

Specification of the desired behavior of the service.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#spec-and-status

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts`

`boolean`

allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts defines if NodePorts will be automatically
allocated for services with type LoadBalancer.  Default is "true". It
may be set to "false" if the cluster load-balancer does not rely on
NodePorts.  If the caller requests specific NodePorts (by specifying a
value), those requests will be respected, regardless of this field.
This field may only be set for services with type LoadBalancer and will
be cleared if the type is changed to any other type.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.clusterIP`

`string`

clusterIP is the IP address of the service and is usually assigned
randomly. If an address is specified manually, is in-range (as per
system configuration), and is not in use, it will be allocated to the
service; otherwise creation of the service will fail. This field may not
be changed through updates unless the type field is also being changed
to ExternalName (which requires this field to be blank) or the type
field is being changed from ExternalName (in which case this field may
optionally be specified, as describe above).  Valid values are "None",
empty string (""), or a valid IP address. Setting this to "None" makes a
"headless service" (no virtual IP), which is useful when direct endpoint
connections are preferred and proxying is not required.  Only applies to
types ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer. If this field is specified
when creating a Service of type ExternalName, creation will fail. This
field will be wiped when updating a Service to type ExternalName.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#virtual-ips-and-service-proxies

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.clusterIPs`

`[]string`

ClusterIPs is a list of IP addresses assigned to this service, and are
usually assigned randomly.  If an address is specified manually, is
in-range (as per system configuration), and is not in use, it will be
allocated to the service; otherwise creation of the service will fail.
This field may not be changed through updates unless the type field is
also being changed to ExternalName (which requires this field to be
empty) or the type field is being changed from ExternalName (in which
case this field may optionally be specified, as describe above).  Valid
values are "None", empty string (""), or a valid IP address.  Setting
this to "None" makes a "headless service" (no virtual IP), which is
useful when direct endpoint connections are preferred and proxying is
not required.  Only applies to types ClusterIP, NodePort, and
LoadBalancer. If this field is specified when creating a Service of type
ExternalName, creation will fail. This field will be wiped when updating
a Service to type ExternalName.  If this field is not specified, it will
be initialized from the clusterIP field.  If this field is specified,
clients must ensure that clusterIPs\[0\] and clusterIP have the same
value.

This field may hold a maximum of two entries (dual-stack IPs, in either order).
These IPs must correspond to the values of the ipFamilies field. Both
clusterIPs and ipFamilies are governed by the ipFamilyPolicy field.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#virtual-ips-and-service-proxies

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.externalIPs`

`[]string`

externalIPs is a list of IP addresses for which nodes in the cluster
will also accept traffic for this service.  These IPs are not managed by
Kubernetes.  The user is responsible for ensuring that traffic arrives
at a node with this IP.  A common example is external load-balancers
that are not part of the Kubernetes system.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.externalName`

`string`

externalName is the external reference that discovery mechanisms will
return as an alias for this service (e.g. a DNS CNAME record). No
proxying will be involved.  Must be a lowercase RFC-1123 hostname
(https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1123) and requires `type` to be "ExternalName".

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.externalTrafficPolicy`

`string`

externalTrafficPolicy describes how nodes distribute service traffic they
receive on one of the Service's "externally-facing" addresses (NodePorts,
ExternalIPs, and LoadBalancer IPs). If set to "Local", the proxy will configure
the service in a way that assumes that external load balancers will take care
of balancing the service traffic between nodes, and so each node will deliver
traffic only to the node-local endpoints of the service, without masquerading
the client source IP. (Traffic mistakenly sent to a node with no endpoints will
be dropped.) The default value, "Cluster", uses the standard behavior of
routing to all endpoints evenly (possibly modified by topology and other
features). Note that traffic sent to an External IP or LoadBalancer IP from
within the cluster will always get "Cluster" semantics, but clients sending to
a NodePort from within the cluster may need to take traffic policy into account
when picking a node.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.healthCheckNodePort`

`integer (int32)`

healthCheckNodePort specifies the healthcheck nodePort for the service.
This only applies when type is set to LoadBalancer and
externalTrafficPolicy is set to Local. If a value is specified, is
in-range, and is not in use, it will be used.  If not specified, a value
will be automatically allocated.  External systems (e.g. load-balancers)
can use this port to determine if a given node holds endpoints for this
service or not.  If this field is specified when creating a Service
which does not need it, creation will fail. This field will be wiped
when updating a Service to no longer need it (e.g. changing type).
This field cannot be updated once set.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.internalTrafficPolicy`

`string`

InternalTrafficPolicy describes how nodes distribute service traffic they
receive on the ClusterIP. If set to "Local", the proxy will assume that pods
only want to talk to endpoints of the service on the same node as the pod,
dropping the traffic if there are no local endpoints. The default value,
"Cluster", uses the standard behavior of routing to all endpoints evenly
(possibly modified by topology and other features).

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ipFamilies`

`[]string`

IPFamilies is a list of IP families (e.g. IPv4, IPv6) assigned to this
service. This field is usually assigned automatically based on cluster
configuration and the ipFamilyPolicy field. If this field is specified
manually, the requested family is available in the cluster,
and ipFamilyPolicy allows it, it will be used; otherwise creation of
the service will fail. This field is conditionally mutable: it allows
for adding or removing a secondary IP family, but it does not allow
changing the primary IP family of the Service. Valid values are "IPv4"
and "IPv6".  This field only applies to Services of types ClusterIP,
NodePort, and LoadBalancer, and does apply to "headless" services.
This field will be wiped when updating a Service to type ExternalName.

This field may hold a maximum of two entries (dual-stack families, in
either order).  These families must correspond to the values of the
clusterIPs field, if specified. Both clusterIPs and ipFamilies are
governed by the ipFamilyPolicy field.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ipFamilyPolicy`

`string`

IPFamilyPolicy represents the dual-stack-ness requested or required by
this Service. If there is no value provided, then this field will be set
to SingleStack. Services can be "SingleStack" (a single IP family),
"PreferDualStack" (two IP families on dual-stack configured clusters or
a single IP family on single-stack clusters), or "RequireDualStack"
(two IP families on dual-stack configured clusters, otherwise fail). The
ipFamilies and clusterIPs fields depend on the value of this field. This
field will be wiped when updating a service to type ExternalName.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.loadBalancerClass`

`string`

loadBalancerClass is the class of the load balancer implementation this Service belongs to.
If specified, the value of this field must be a label-style identifier, with an optional prefix,
e.g. "internal-vip" or "example.com/internal-vip". Unprefixed names are reserved for end-users.
This field can only be set when the Service type is 'LoadBalancer'. If not set, the default load
balancer implementation is used, today this is typically done through the cloud provider integration,
but should apply for any default implementation. If set, it is assumed that a load balancer
implementation is watching for Services with a matching class. Any default load balancer
implementation (e.g. cloud providers) should ignore Services that set this field.
This field can only be set when creating or updating a Service to type 'LoadBalancer'.
Once set, it can not be changed. This field will be wiped when a service is updated to a non 'LoadBalancer' type.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.loadBalancerIP`

`string`

Only applies to Service Type: LoadBalancer.
This feature depends on whether the underlying cloud-provider supports specifying
the loadBalancerIP when a load balancer is created.
This field will be ignored if the cloud-provider does not support the feature.
Deprecated: This field was under-specified and its meaning varies across implementations.
Using it is non-portable and it may not support dual-stack.
Users are encouraged to use implementation-specific annotations when available.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges`

`[]string`

If specified and supported by the platform, this will restrict traffic through the cloud-provider
load-balancer will be restricted to the specified client IPs. This field will be ignored if the
cloud-provider does not support the feature."
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-application-cluster/create-external-load-balancer/

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ports`

`[]object`

The list of ports that are exposed by this service.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#virtual-ips-and-service-proxies

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ports[].appProtocol`

`string`

The application protocol for this port.
This is used as a hint for implementations to offer richer behavior for protocols that they understand.
This field follows standard Kubernetes label syntax.
Valid values are either:

- Un-prefixed protocol names - reserved for IANA standard service names (as per

RFC-6335 and https://www.iana.org/assignments/service-names).

- Kubernetes-defined prefixed names:
  - 'kubernetes.io/h2c' - HTTP/2 prior knowledge over cleartext as described in https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9113.html#name-starting-http-2-with-prior-
  - 'kubernetes.io/ws'  - WebSocket over cleartext as described in https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455
  - 'kubernetes.io/wss' - WebSocket over TLS as described in https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455

- Other protocols should use implementation-defined prefixed names such as

mycompany.com/my-custom-protocol.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ports[].name`

`string`

The name of this port within the service. This must be a DNS_LABEL.
All ports within a ServiceSpec must have unique names. When considering
the endpoints for a Service, this must match the 'name' field in the
EndpointPort.
Optional if only one ServicePort is defined on this service.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ports[].nodePort`

`integer (int32)`

The port on each node on which this service is exposed when type is
NodePort or LoadBalancer.  Usually assigned by the system. If a value is
specified, in-range, and not in use it will be used, otherwise the
operation will fail.  If not specified, a port will be allocated if this
Service requires one.  If this field is specified when creating a
Service which does not need it, creation will fail. This field will be
wiped when updating a Service to no longer need it (e.g. changing type
from NodePort to ClusterIP).
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#type-nodeport

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ports[].port`

`integer (int32)` · required

The port that will be exposed by this service.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ports[].protocol`

`string` · default `"TCP"`

The IP protocol for this port. Supports "TCP", "UDP", and "SCTP".
Default is TCP.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.ports[].targetPort`

`integer or string`

Number or name of the port to access on the pods targeted by the service.
Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
If this is a string, it will be looked up as a named port in the
target Pod's container ports. If this is not specified, the value
of the 'port' field is used (an identity map).
This field is ignored for services with clusterIP=None, and should be
omitted or set equal to the 'port' field.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#defining-a-service

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.publishNotReadyAddresses`

`boolean`

publishNotReadyAddresses indicates that any agent which deals with endpoints for this
Service should disregard any indications of ready/not-ready.
The primary use case for setting this field is for a StatefulSet's Headless Service to
propagate SRV DNS records for its Pods for the purpose of peer discovery.
The Kubernetes controllers that generate Endpoints and EndpointSlice resources for
Services interpret this to mean that all endpoints are considered "ready" even if the
Pods themselves are not. Agents which consume only Kubernetes generated endpoints
through the Endpoints or EndpointSlice resources can safely assume this behavior.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.selector`

`map[string]string`

Route service traffic to pods with label keys and values matching this
selector. If empty or not present, the service is assumed to have an
external process managing its endpoints, which Kubernetes will not
modify. Only applies to types ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer.
Ignored if type is ExternalName.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.sessionAffinity`

`string`

Supports "ClientIP" and "None". Used to maintain session affinity.
Enable client IP based session affinity.
Must be ClientIP or None.
Defaults to None.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#virtual-ips-and-service-proxies

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.sessionAffinityConfig`

`object`

sessionAffinityConfig contains the configurations of session affinity.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP`

`object`

clientIP contains the configurations of Client IP based session affinity.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds`

`integer (int32)`

timeoutSeconds specifies the seconds of ClientIP type session sticky time.
The value must be &gt;0 && &lt;=86400(for 1 day) if ServiceAffinity == "ClientIP".
Default value is 10800(for 3 hours).

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.trafficDistribution`

`string`

TrafficDistribution offers a way to express preferences for how traffic
is distributed to Service endpoints. Implementations can use this field
as a hint, but are not required to guarantee strict adherence. If the
field is not set, the implementation will apply its default routing
strategy. If set to "PreferClose", implementations should prioritize
endpoints that are in the same zone.

#### `managed.services.additional[].serviceTemplate.spec.type`

`string`

type determines how the Service is exposed. Defaults to ClusterIP. Valid
options are ExternalName, ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer.
"ClusterIP" allocates a cluster-internal IP address for load-balancing
to endpoints. Endpoints are determined by the selector or if that is not
specified, by manual construction of an Endpoints object or
EndpointSlice objects. If clusterIP is "None", no virtual IP is
allocated and the endpoints are published as a set of endpoints rather
than a virtual IP.
"NodePort" builds on ClusterIP and allocates a port on every node which
routes to the same endpoints as the clusterIP.
"LoadBalancer" builds on NodePort and creates an external load-balancer
(if supported in the current cloud) which routes to the same endpoints
as the clusterIP.
"ExternalName" aliases this service to the specified externalName.
Several other fields do not apply to ExternalName services.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#publishing-services-service-types

#### `managed.services.additional[].updateStrategy`

`string` · default `"patch"` · one of `patch`, `replace`

UpdateStrategy describes how the service differences should be reconciled

#### `managed.services.disabledDefaultServices`

`[]string`

DisabledDefaultServices is a list of service types that are disabled by default.
Valid values are "r", and "ro", representing read, and read-only services.

### `monitoring`

`object`

Monitoring configures CNPG's metrics exporter on port 9187 of every
instance pod: custom queries, the default queries, TLS and relabeling.
The provider adds the queries of pg_stat_statements when that extension
is enabled. To have the Prometheus Operator scrape the instance, use
spec.topology.parameters.monitoring.prometheus instead of the deprecated
enablePodMonitor, which cannot be combined with it.

#### `monitoring.customQueriesConfigMap`

`[]object`

The list of config maps containing the custom queries

#### `monitoring.customQueriesConfigMap[].key`

`string` · required

The key to select

#### `monitoring.customQueriesConfigMap[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `monitoring.customQueriesSecret`

`[]object`

The list of secrets containing the custom queries

#### `monitoring.customQueriesSecret[].key`

`string` · required

The key to select

#### `monitoring.customQueriesSecret[].name`

`string` · required

Name of the referent.

#### `monitoring.disableDefaultQueries`

`boolean` · default `false`

Whether the default queries should be injected.
Set it to `true` if you don't want to inject default queries into the cluster.
Default: false.

#### `monitoring.enablePodMonitor`

`boolean` · default `false`

Enable or disable the `PodMonitor`

Deprecated: This feature will be removed in an upcoming release. If
you need this functionality, you can create a PodMonitor manually.

#### `monitoring.metricsQueriesTTL`

`string`

The interval during which metrics computed from queries are considered current.
Once it is exceeded, a new scrape will trigger a rerun
of the queries.
If not set, defaults to 30 seconds, in line with Prometheus scraping defaults.
Setting this to zero disables the caching mechanism and can cause heavy load on the PostgreSQL server.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorMetricRelabelings`

`[]object`

The list of metric relabelings for the `PodMonitor`. Applied to samples before ingestion.

Deprecated: This feature will be removed in an upcoming release. If
you need this functionality, you can create a PodMonitor manually.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorMetricRelabelings[].action`

`string` · default `"replace"` · one of `replace`, `Replace`, `keep`, `Keep`, `drop`, `Drop`, `hashmod`, `HashMod`, `labelmap`, `LabelMap`, `labeldrop`, `LabelDrop`, `labelkeep`, `LabelKeep`, `lowercase`, `Lowercase`, `uppercase`, `Uppercase`, `keepequal`, `KeepEqual`, `dropequal`, `DropEqual`

action to perform based on the regex matching.

`Uppercase` and `Lowercase` actions require Prometheus &gt;= v2.36.0.
`DropEqual` and `KeepEqual` actions require Prometheus &gt;= v2.41.0.

Default: "Replace"

#### `monitoring.podMonitorMetricRelabelings[].modulus`

`integer (int64)` · minimum 0

modulus to take of the hash of the source label values.

Only applicable when the action is `HashMod`.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorMetricRelabelings[].regex`

`string`

regex defines the regular expression against which the extracted value is matched.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorMetricRelabelings[].replacement`

`string`

replacement value against which a Replace action is performed if the
regular expression matches.

Regex capture groups are available.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorMetricRelabelings[].separator`

`string`

separator defines the string between concatenated SourceLabels.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorMetricRelabelings[].sourceLabels`

`[]string`

sourceLabels defines the source labels select values from existing labels. Their content is
concatenated using the configured Separator and matched against the
configured regular expression.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorMetricRelabelings[].targetLabel`

`string`

targetLabel defines the label to which the resulting string is written in a replacement.

It is mandatory for `Replace`, `HashMod`, `Lowercase`, `Uppercase`,
`KeepEqual` and `DropEqual` actions.

Regex capture groups are available.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorRelabelings`

`[]object`

The list of relabelings for the `PodMonitor`. Applied to samples before scraping.

Deprecated: This feature will be removed in an upcoming release. If
you need this functionality, you can create a PodMonitor manually.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorRelabelings[].action`

`string` · default `"replace"` · one of `replace`, `Replace`, `keep`, `Keep`, `drop`, `Drop`, `hashmod`, `HashMod`, `labelmap`, `LabelMap`, `labeldrop`, `LabelDrop`, `labelkeep`, `LabelKeep`, `lowercase`, `Lowercase`, `uppercase`, `Uppercase`, `keepequal`, `KeepEqual`, `dropequal`, `DropEqual`

action to perform based on the regex matching.

`Uppercase` and `Lowercase` actions require Prometheus &gt;= v2.36.0.
`DropEqual` and `KeepEqual` actions require Prometheus &gt;= v2.41.0.

Default: "Replace"

#### `monitoring.podMonitorRelabelings[].modulus`

`integer (int64)` · minimum 0

modulus to take of the hash of the source label values.

Only applicable when the action is `HashMod`.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorRelabelings[].regex`

`string`

regex defines the regular expression against which the extracted value is matched.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorRelabelings[].replacement`

`string`

replacement value against which a Replace action is performed if the
regular expression matches.

Regex capture groups are available.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorRelabelings[].separator`

`string`

separator defines the string between concatenated SourceLabels.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorRelabelings[].sourceLabels`

`[]string`

sourceLabels defines the source labels select values from existing labels. Their content is
concatenated using the configured Separator and matched against the
configured regular expression.

#### `monitoring.podMonitorRelabelings[].targetLabel`

`string`

targetLabel defines the label to which the resulting string is written in a replacement.

It is mandatory for `Replace`, `HashMod`, `Lowercase`, `Uppercase`,
`KeepEqual` and `DropEqual` actions.

Regex capture groups are available.

#### `monitoring.tls`

`object`

Configure TLS communication for the metrics endpoint.
Changing tls.enabled option will force a rollout of all instances.

#### `monitoring.tls.enabled`

`boolean` · default `false`

Enable TLS for the monitoring endpoint.
Changing this option will force a rollout of all instances.

### `pgHBA`

`string`

PgHBA declares which clients may connect to which databases as which
users: pg_hba.conf records, one per line, such as

```text
hostssl orders orders_app 10.0.0.0/8 scram-sha-256
host    orders all        all        reject
```

Blank lines and # comments are ignored. Records are checked in order,
after the operator's own rules (replication, pooler, metrics) and before
the default rule that lets every user in with a password, so end with a
reject record to allow only what is listed. Records may be host, hostssl
or hostnossl with the methods scram-sha-256, md5, cert, ldap, radius or
reject; trust is not allowed. Cannot be combined with postgresql.pg_hba.
Applied by CNPG with a configuration reload, no restart.

### `postgresql`

`object`

PostgreSQL is CNPG's PostgreSQL configuration: parameters
(postgresql.conf), pg_hba and pg_ident records, synchronous
replication, shared_preload_libraries, LDAP and more. CNPG manages a
fixed set of parameters itself and rejects them here. The provider adds
the records of requireTLS and pgHBA, the parameters and libraries of
enabled extensions and replication slot settings. pg_hba cannot be
combined with pgHBA. CNPG reloads PostgreSQL, or restarts the instances
for parameters that need it.

#### `postgresql.enableAlterSystem`

`boolean`

If this parameter is true, the user will be able to invoke `ALTER SYSTEM`
on this CloudNativePG Cluster.
This should only be used for debugging and troubleshooting.
Defaults to false.

#### `postgresql.extensions`

`[]object`

The configuration of the extensions to be added

#### `postgresql.extensions[].bin_path`

`[]string`

A list of directories within the image to be appended to the
PostgreSQL process's `PATH` environment variable.

#### `postgresql.extensions[].dynamic_library_path`

`[]string`

The list of directories inside the image which should be added to dynamic_library_path.
If not defined, defaults to "/lib".

#### `postgresql.extensions[].env`

`[]object`

Env is a list of custom environment variables to be set in the
PostgreSQL process for this extension. It is the responsibility of the
cluster administrator to ensure the variables are correct for the
specific extension. Note that changes to these variables require
a manual cluster restart to take effect.

#### `postgresql.extensions[].env[].name`

`string` · required · at least 1 characters · pattern `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`

Name of the environment variable to be injected into the
PostgreSQL process.

#### `postgresql.extensions[].env[].value`

`string` · required · at least 1 characters

Value of the environment variable. CloudNativePG performs a direct
replacement of this value, with support for placeholder expansion.
The ${`image_root`} placeholder resolves to the absolute mount path
of the extension's volume (e.g., `/extensions/my-extension`). This
is particularly useful for allowing applications or libraries to
locate specific directories within the mounted image.
Unrecognized placeholders are rejected. To include a literal ${...}
in the value, escape it as $${...}.

#### `postgresql.extensions[].extension_control_path`

`[]string`

The list of directories inside the image which should be added to extension_control_path.
If not defined, defaults to "/share".

#### `postgresql.extensions[].image`

`object`

The image containing the extension.

#### `postgresql.extensions[].image.pullPolicy`

`string`

Policy for pulling OCI objects. Possible values are:
Always: the kubelet always attempts to pull the reference. Container creation will fail If the pull fails.
Never: the kubelet never pulls the reference and only uses a local image or artifact. Container creation will fail if the reference isn't present.
IfNotPresent: the kubelet pulls if the reference isn't already present on disk. Container creation will fail if the reference isn't present and the pull fails.
Defaults to Always if :latest tag is specified, or IfNotPresent otherwise.

#### `postgresql.extensions[].image.reference`

`string`

Required: Image or artifact reference to be used.
Behaves in the same way as pod.spec.containers\[\*\].image.
Pull secrets will be assembled in the same way as for the container image by looking up node credentials, SA image pull secrets, and pod spec image pull secrets.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images
This field is optional to allow higher level config management to default or override
container images in workload controllers like Deployments and StatefulSets.

#### `postgresql.extensions[].ld_library_path`

`[]string`

The list of directories inside the image which should be added to ld_library_path.

#### `postgresql.extensions[].name`

`string` · required · at least 1 characters · at most 59 characters · pattern `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9_]*[a-z0-9])?$`

The name of the extension, required. The limit of 59 characters
leaves room for the prefix the operator adds when deriving the
extension's Kubernetes Volume name (capped at 63 characters).

#### `postgresql.ldap`

`object`

Options to specify LDAP configuration

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindAsAuth`

`object`

Bind as authentication configuration

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindAsAuth.prefix`

`string`

Prefix for the bind authentication option

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindAsAuth.suffix`

`string`

Suffix for the bind authentication option

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth`

`object`

Bind+Search authentication configuration

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth.baseDN`

`string`

Root DN to begin the user search

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth.bindDN`

`string`

DN of the user to bind to the directory

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth.bindPassword`

`object`

Secret with the password for the user to bind to the directory

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth.bindPassword.key`

`string` · required

The key of the secret to select from.  Must be a valid secret key.

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth.bindPassword.name`

`string` · default `""`

Name of the referent.
This field is effectively required, but due to backwards compatibility is
allowed to be empty. Instances of this type with an empty value here are
almost certainly wrong.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth.bindPassword.optional`

`boolean`

Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth.searchAttribute`

`string`

Attribute to match against the username

#### `postgresql.ldap.bindSearchAuth.searchFilter`

`string`

Search filter to use when doing the search+bind authentication

#### `postgresql.ldap.port`

`integer`

LDAP server port

#### `postgresql.ldap.scheme`

`string` · one of `ldap`, `ldaps`

LDAP schema to be used, possible options are `ldap` and `ldaps`

#### `postgresql.ldap.server`

`string`

LDAP hostname or IP address

#### `postgresql.ldap.tls`

`boolean`

Set to 'true' to enable LDAP over TLS. 'false' is default

#### `postgresql.parameters`

`map[string]string`

PostgreSQL configuration options (postgresql.conf)

#### `postgresql.pg_hba`

`[]string`

PostgreSQL Host Based Authentication rules (lines to be appended
to the pg_hba.conf file).
Use the ${podselector:NAME} syntax to reference a pod selector;
the rule will be expanded for each Pod IP matching that selector.

#### `postgresql.pg_ident`

`[]string`

PostgreSQL User Name Maps rules (lines to be appended
to the pg_ident.conf file)

#### `postgresql.promotionTimeout`

`integer (int32)`

Specifies the maximum number of seconds to wait when promoting an instance to primary.
Default value is 40000000, greater than one year in seconds,
big enough to simulate an infinite timeout

#### `postgresql.shared_preload_libraries`

`[]string`

Lists of shared preload libraries to add to the default ones

#### `postgresql.syncReplicaElectionConstraint`

`object`

Requirements to be met by sync replicas. This will affect how the "synchronous_standby_names" parameter will be
set up.

#### `postgresql.syncReplicaElectionConstraint.enabled`

`boolean` · required

This flag enables the constraints for sync replicas

#### `postgresql.syncReplicaElectionConstraint.nodeLabelsAntiAffinity`

`[]string`

A list of node labels values to extract and compare to evaluate if the pods reside in the same topology or not

#### `postgresql.synchronous`

`object`

Configuration of the PostgreSQL synchronous replication feature

- Rule: dataDurability set to 'preferred' requires empty 'standbyNamesPre' and empty 'standbyNamesPost' (`self.dataDurability!='preferred' || ((!has(self.standbyNamesPre) || self.standbyNamesPre.size()==0) && (!has(self.standbyNamesPost) || self.standbyNamesPost.size()==0))`)

#### `postgresql.synchronous.dataDurability`

`string` · one of `required`, `preferred`

If set to "required", data durability is strictly enforced. Write operations
with synchronous commit settings (`on`, `remote_write`, or `remote_apply`) will
block if there are insufficient healthy replicas, ensuring data persistence.
If set to "preferred", data durability is maintained when healthy replicas
are available, but the required number of instances will adjust dynamically
if replicas become unavailable. This setting relaxes strict durability enforcement
to allow for operational continuity. This setting is only applicable if both
`standbyNamesPre` and `standbyNamesPost` are unset (empty).

#### `postgresql.synchronous.failoverQuorum`

`boolean`

FailoverQuorum enables a quorum-based check before failover, improving
data durability and safety during failover events in CloudNativePG-managed
PostgreSQL clusters.

#### `postgresql.synchronous.maxStandbyNamesFromCluster`

`integer`

Specifies the maximum number of local cluster pods that can be
automatically included in the `synchronous_standby_names` option in
PostgreSQL.

#### `postgresql.synchronous.method`

`string` · required · one of `any`, `first`

Method to select synchronous replication standbys from the listed
servers, accepting 'any' (quorum-based synchronous replication) or
'first' (priority-based synchronous replication) as values.

#### `postgresql.synchronous.number`

`integer` · required

Specifies the number of synchronous standby servers that
transactions must wait for responses from.

- Rule: The number of synchronous replicas should be greater than zero (`self > 0`)

#### `postgresql.synchronous.standbyNamesPost`

`[]string`

A user-defined list of application names to be added to
`synchronous_standby_names` after local cluster pods (the order is
only useful for priority-based synchronous replication).

#### `postgresql.synchronous.standbyNamesPre`

`[]string`

A user-defined list of application names to be added to
`synchronous_standby_names` before local cluster pods (the order is
only useful for priority-based synchronous replication).

### `priorityClassName`

`string`

PriorityClassName sets the Kubernetes PriorityClass of the instance pods.
The PriorityClass must exist; changing it rolls the instance pods.

### `pvcTemplate`

`object`

PVCTemplate is the template of the data volumes' PersistentVolumeClaims
(CNPG storage.pvcTemplate), for settings the Instance doesn't have, such
as accessModes or volumeAttributesClassName. The engine's storage size
and storageClass take precedence over the template's.

#### `pvcTemplate.accessModes`

`[]string`

accessModes contains the desired access modes the volume should have.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#access-modes-1

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSource`

`object`
