dataSource field can be used to specify either:
- An existing VolumeSnapshot object (snapshot.storage.k8s.io/VolumeSnapshot)
- An existing PVC (PersistentVolumeClaim)

If the provisioner or an external controller can support the specified data source,
it will create a new volume based on the contents of the specified data source.
dataSource contents will be copied to dataSourceRef, and dataSourceRef contents will be
copied to dataSource when dataSourceRef.namespace is not specified.
If the namespace is specified, then dataSourceRef will not be copied to dataSource.

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSource.apiGroup`

`string`

APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced.
If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group.
For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSource.kind`

`string` · required

Kind is the type of resource being referenced

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSource.name`

`string` · required

Name is the name of resource being referenced

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSourceRef`

`object`

dataSourceRef specifies the object from which to populate the volume with data, if a non-empty
volume is desired. This may be any object from a non-empty API group (non
core object) or a PersistentVolumeClaim object.
When this field is specified, volume binding will only succeed if the type of
the specified object matches some installed volume populator or dynamic
provisioner.
This field will replace the functionality of the dataSource field and as such
if both fields are non-empty, they must have the same value. For backwards
compatibility, when namespace isn't specified in dataSourceRef,
both fields (dataSource and dataSourceRef) will be set to the same
value automatically if one of them is empty and the other is non-empty.
When namespace is specified in dataSourceRef,
dataSource isn't set to the same value and must be empty.
There are three important differences between dataSource and dataSourceRef:
- While dataSource only allows two specific types of objects, dataSourceRef
  allows any non-core object, as well as PersistentVolumeClaim objects.
- While dataSource ignores disallowed values (dropping them), dataSourceRef
  preserves all values, and generates an error if a disallowed value is
  specified.
- While dataSource only allows local objects, dataSourceRef allows objects
  in any namespaces.

(Alpha) Using the namespace field of dataSourceRef requires the CrossNamespaceVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSourceRef.apiGroup`

`string`

APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced.
If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group.
For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSourceRef.kind`

`string` · required

Kind is the type of resource being referenced

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSourceRef.name`

`string` · required

Name is the name of resource being referenced

#### `pvcTemplate.dataSourceRef.namespace`

`string`

Namespace is the namespace of resource being referenced
Note that when a namespace is specified, a gateway.networking.k8s.io/ReferenceGrant object is required in the referent namespace to allow that namespace's owner to accept the reference. See the ReferenceGrant documentation for details.
(Alpha) This field requires the CrossNamespaceVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.

#### `pvcTemplate.resources`

`object`

resources represents the minimum resources the volume should have.
Users are allowed to specify resource requirements
that are lower than previous value but must still be higher than capacity recorded in the
status field of the claim.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#resources

#### `pvcTemplate.resources.limits`

`map[string]integer or string`

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

#### `pvcTemplate.resources.requests`

`map[string]integer or string`

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required.
If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified,
otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

#### `pvcTemplate.selector`

`object`

selector is a label query over volumes to consider for binding.

#### `pvcTemplate.selector.matchExpressions`

`[]object`

matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed.

#### `pvcTemplate.selector.matchExpressions[].key`

`string` · required

key is the label key that the selector applies to.

#### `pvcTemplate.selector.matchExpressions[].operator`

`string` · required

operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

#### `pvcTemplate.selector.matchExpressions[].values`

`[]string`

values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. This array is replaced during a strategic
merge patch.

#### `pvcTemplate.selector.matchLabels`

`map[string]string`

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels
map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the
operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

#### `pvcTemplate.storageClassName`

`string`

storageClassName is the name of the StorageClass required by the claim.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#class-1

#### `pvcTemplate.volumeAttributesClassName`

`string`

volumeAttributesClassName may be used to set the VolumeAttributesClass used by this claim.
If specified, the CSI driver will create or update the volume with the attributes defined
in the corresponding VolumeAttributesClass. This has a different purpose than storageClassName,
it can be changed after the claim is created. An empty string or nil value indicates that no
VolumeAttributesClass will be applied to the claim. If the claim enters an Infeasible error state,
this field can be reset to its previous value (including nil) to cancel the modification.
If the resource referred to by volumeAttributesClass does not exist, this PersistentVolumeClaim will be
set to a Pending state, as reflected by the modifyVolumeStatus field, until such as a resource
exists.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-attributes-classes/

#### `pvcTemplate.volumeMode`

`string`

volumeMode defines what type of volume is required by the claim.
Value of Filesystem is implied when not included in claim spec.

#### `pvcTemplate.volumeName`

`string`

volumeName is the binding reference to the PersistentVolume backing this claim.

### `replicationSlots`

`object`

ReplicationSlots configures CNPG replication slots: the physical slots of
the HA standbys, synchronization of user-defined physical slots to the
standbys, and failover of logical decoding slots
(highAvailability.synchronizeLogicalDecoding). With synchronizeLogicalDecoding
on PostgreSQL 17+, the provider turns on hot_standby_feedback and
sync_replication_slots unless they are set explicitly.
highAvailability.slotPrefix cannot change while HA slots are enabled.

#### `replicationSlots.highAvailability`

`object` · default `{"enabled":true}`

Replication slots for high availability configuration

#### `replicationSlots.highAvailability.enabled`

`boolean` · default `true`

If enabled (default), the operator will automatically manage replication slots
on the primary instance and use them in streaming replication
connections with all the standby instances that are part of the HA
cluster. If disabled, the operator will not take advantage
of replication slots in streaming connections with the replicas.
This feature also controls replication slots in replica cluster,
from the designated primary to its cascading replicas.

#### `replicationSlots.highAvailability.slotPrefix`

`string` · default `"_cnpg_"` · pattern `^[0-9a-z_]*$`

Prefix for replication slots managed by the operator for HA.
It may only contain lower case letters, numbers, and the underscore character.
This can only be set at creation time. By default set to `_cnpg_`.

#### `replicationSlots.highAvailability.synchronizeLogicalDecoding`

`boolean`

When enabled, the operator automatically manages synchronization of logical
decoding (replication) slots across high-availability clusters.

Requires one of the following conditions:
- PostgreSQL version 17 or later
- PostgreSQL version &lt; 17 with pg_failover_slots extension enabled

#### `replicationSlots.synchronizeReplicas`

`object`

Configures the synchronization of the user defined physical replication slots

#### `replicationSlots.synchronizeReplicas.enabled`

`boolean` · required · default `true`

When set to true, every replication slot that is on the primary is synchronized on each standby

#### `replicationSlots.synchronizeReplicas.excludePatterns`

`[]string`

List of regular expression patterns to match the names of replication slots to be excluded (by default empty)

#### `replicationSlots.updateInterval`

`integer` · default `30` · minimum 1

Standby will update the status of the local replication slots
every `updateInterval` seconds (default 30).

### `requireTLS`

`boolean`

RequireTLS rejects client connections that do not use TLS by placing a
"hostnossl all all all reject" rule before the user's pg_hba rules.
Unset or false keeps CNPG's default, which also accepts unencrypted
connections. Applied by CNPG with a configuration reload, no restart.

### `resizeInUseVolumes`

`boolean`

ResizeInUseVolumes lets CNPG grow the data volumes of running instances
when the engine's storage size increases; the StorageClass must allow
volume expansion. Unset keeps CNPG's default, true.

### `tls`

`object`

TLS sets the server certificate PostgreSQL and PgBouncer present to
clients: one a cert-manager issuer signs, or one in a Secret. Without
it CNPG issues the certificate from a CA it creates for the instance.
Its issuer and certificateSecretName cannot be combined with the server
fields of certificates.

#### `tls.certificateSecretName`

`string`

CertificateSecretName is a Secret in the instance's namespace holding
the server certificate, followed by any intermediate CA certificates
(tls.crt), its private key (tls.key) and the CA certificate clients
verify the server with (ca.crt). The certificate must be valid for the
names clients connect to, such as &lt;instance&gt;-rw.&lt;namespace&gt;.svc. The
provider labels the Secret cnpg.io/reload, so PostgreSQL loads a
renewed certificate without a restart.

#### `tls.extraDNSNames`

`[]string`

ExtraDNSNames are names the server certificate is valid for besides
those of the instance's Services, such as an external DNS name. Used
with issuer, or without issuer and certificateSecretName for the
certificate CNPG issues. Cannot be combined with certificateSecretName,
whose certificate carries its own names.

#### `tls.issuer`

`object`

Issuer is the cert-manager Issuer or ClusterIssuer that signs the
server certificate. The provider requests it as the Certificate
&lt;instance&gt;-tls, for every name of the instance's Services and those of
extraDNSNames, and cert-manager renews it. The issuer must write its CA
certificate to the Secret's ca.crt, as the CA and Vault issuers do;
clients verify the server with it. Needs cert-manager.

#### `tls.issuer.group`

`string`

Group is the API group of an external issuer, such as
awspca.cert-manager.io. Defaults to cert-manager.io.

#### `tls.issuer.kind`

`string`

Kind of the issuer: Issuer (the default) or ClusterIssuer, or the kind
of an external issuer of group.

#### `tls.issuer.name`

`string` · required

Name of the issuer. An Issuer must be in the instance's namespace.

### `walStorage`

`object`

WALStorage provisions a separate WAL PVC per PostgreSQL instance using
CNPG's native storage configuration. Once enabled it cannot be removed.

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.accessModes`

More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#access-modes-1

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.dataSource.apiGroup`

If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group.
For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.dataSource.kind`

`string` · required

Kind is the type of resource being referenced

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.dataSource.name`

(Alpha) Using the namespace field of dataSourceRef requires the CrossNamespaceVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.dataSourceRef.apiGroup`

`string`

APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced.
If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group.
For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.dataSourceRef.kind`

`string` · required

Kind is the type of resource being referenced

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.dataSourceRef.name`

`string` · required

Name is the name of resource being referenced

`string`

Namespace is the namespace of resource being referenced

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.resources`

`object`

resources represents the minimum resources the volume should have.
Users are allowed to specify resource requirements
that are lower than previous value but must still be higher than capacity recorded in the

this field can be reset to its previous value (including nil) to cancel the modification.
If the resource referred to by volumeAttributesClass does not exist, this PersistentVolumeClaim will be
set to a Pending state, as reflected by the modifyVolumeStatus field, until such as a resource

`string`

#### `walStorage.pvcTemplate.volumeName`

`string`

volumeName is the binding reference to the PersistentVolume backing this claim.

#### `walStorage.resizeInUseVolumes`

`boolean` · default `true`

Resize existent PVCs, defaults to true

#### `walStorage.size`

`string`

Size of the storage. Required if not already specified in the PVC template.
Changes to this field are automatically reapplied to the created PVCs.
Size cannot be decreased.

#### `walStorage.storageClass`

`string`

StorageClass to use for PVCs. Applied after
evaluating the PVC template, if available.
If not specified, the generated PVCs will use the
default storage class

## Component proxy (pgbouncer)

Set in `spec.components.proxy.parameters` of an Instance.

### `poolMode`

`string`

PoolMode is the PgBouncer pool mode. CloudNativePG accepts session and
transaction. Empty selects the operator default, session.

### `readOnly`

`boolean`

ReadOnly also creates a CloudNativePG Pooler of type ro that forwards to
the replicas. host-ro in the connection Secret then points at that
Pooler's Service. Requires at least two engine replicas, because the
cluster's -ro Service has no endpoints with a single instance.

## Topology replicaSet

Set in `spec.topology.parameters` of an Instance with `spec.topology.type: replicaSet`.

### `monitoring`

`object`

Deprecated: Monitoring has no effect. Metrics are collected by listing
a MonitoringDestination in spec.monitoring.destinations: a monitoring
extension creates the scrape objects. It is still accepted because
Instances created by earlier releases carry it.

#### `monitoring.prometheus`

`object`

Deprecated: Prometheus has no effect.

#### `monitoring.prometheus.enabled`

`boolean`

Deprecated: Enabled has no effect.

#### `monitoring.prometheus.podMonitorLabels`

`map[string]string`

Deprecated: PodMonitorLabels has no effect.

## BackupClass cnpg-barman-plugin: backups

Set in `spec.parameters` of a Backup, and `spec.backup.storages[].schedules[].parameters` of an Instance, with BackupClass `cnpg-barman-plugin`.

### `target`

`string` · one of `primary`, `prefer-standby`

Target overrides the cluster default backup target for this run.
